title: Floor 2: Nowhere zones
task:
Return every row of trips, plus three columns:
- pu_zone and do_zone: the zone name from zones (NULL when there is no match)
- zone_flag: the first label that applies, checking both pu_location_id and do_location_id:
  1. 'unmatched' if either id is NULL or not in zones
  2. 'unknown' if either id is 264
  3. 'outside_nyc' if either id is 265
  4. 'ok' otherwise
dirt:
SELECT row_id, pu_location_id, do_location_id FROM trips
WHERE pu_location_id IS NULL OR do_location_id IS NULL OR pu_location_id IN (264, 265) OR do_location_id IN (264, 265)
   OR pu_location_id NOT IN (SELECT location_id FROM zones) OR do_location_id NOT IN (SELECT location_id FROM zones)
guideTask: return every row of trips, plus three columns: pu_zone, do_zone and zone_flag.
card: Some trips start or end in a zone that is not on the map.
context: The depot needs to report where every trip started and ended, including trips whose locations cannot be matched. trips holds 7,171 trips with rerun copies already removed; zones is the location lookup. Keeping unmatched trips in the report prevents an incomplete picture of service and revenue.

refresher.title: A query in steps: WITH
refresher.text: WITH names a query result so the next step can read it. The final SELECT returns your answer. These steps are one query; you do not need to save a table.
refresher.sql:
WITH rides(id) AS (VALUES (1), (2))
SELECT count(*) AS rides FROM rides;

refresher.title: Keep unmatched rows with LEFT JOIN
refresher.text: A JOIN matches keys between tables. A LEFT JOIN keeps every row on the left and puts NULL in the right columns when there is no match. Aliases such as r and z name the two table copies. Joining twice lets you look up two locations.
refresher.sql:
WITH rides(id, place) AS (VALUES (1, 10), (2, 99)),
places(id, name) AS (VALUES (10, 'Depot'))
SELECT r.id, z.name FROM rides r
LEFT JOIN places z ON z.id = r.place;

refresher.title: Label the first matching condition
refresher.text: CASE tests WHEN conditions in order: the first true branch wins. Here 1 meets both conditions but gets first; 2 gets second, and 3 reaches ELSE. In an answer without ELSE, rows that match no branch get NULL. Test missing values with IS NULL.
refresher.sql:
WITH examples(n) AS (VALUES (1), (2), (3))
SELECT n, CASE WHEN n < 2 THEN 'first'
WHEN n < 3 THEN 'second' ELSE 'other' END AS label
FROM examples;

refresher.title: Count the joined result
refresher.text: COUNT(*) checks that a join kept the expected number of rows. GROUP BY makes one group per label; HAVING can filter those groups. Use a WITH step to name the result you want to count.

rulesText:
## Floor 2: Nowhere zones (joins, NULLs and sentinels)

- **Tables given:** `trips` (floor 1's reference output, 7,171 rows), `zones`.
- **The dirt:** real: 110 trips touch zone 264 "Unknown", 74 touch zone 265 "Outside of NYC".
  Planted: 15 drop-off ids are 0 (not in the lookup) and 10 drop-off ids are NULL.
- **Task:** return an answer: every row of `trips`, plus `pu_zone`, `do_zone` (the zone name,
  NULL when there is no match) and `zone_flag`, the first that applies:
  1. `'unmatched'`: either id is NULL or not in `zones`;
  2. `'unknown'`: either id is 264;
  3. `'outside_nyc'`: either id is 265;
  4. `'ok'`.
- **Expected:** 7,171 rows in and out. Flags: ok 6,962; unknown 110; outside_nyc 74; unmatched 25.
  An inner join to `zones` on both ids keeps only 7,146 rows (it silently loses 25).
- **Pass:** 7,171 rows; the multiset of `(row_id, pu_zone, do_zone, zone_flag)` equals the reference
  `data/reference/floor2.sql`; all columns of `trips` present and unchanged.
- **Aha line:** a join can drop rows without an error. "Unknown" (264) is in the lookup, so an anti-join cannot find it; a missing id (0, NULL) is not, so only a left join shows it. Flag, do not delete.
taskContext: The depot needs location labels without losing trips whose zone ids do not match.

levels: The task panel above Scratch holds the full rules and a checklist for Answer. Open it before writing your query; it starts collapsed on mobile. The checklist shows whether Answer has been run and its last row count. SQL refresher and About the data links beside it open the guide in a new tab.

Use the task panel checklist after each Run answer: an empty Answer result shows zero rows. Scratch table changes never count as an Answer run. Check floor grades your current Answer query; a row count alone does not mean correct. The panel remembers your collapse choice in the page address.

The task panel checklist starts at Answer: not run yet, then reports Answer: N rows (last run). It preserves that last-run count while you edit Answer or use Scratch. Compare it with the full rules; Check floor evaluates the current query independently of the last run.

Under Tables above Scratch, open a table chip to see its columns and types. Start with trips to find the available names before writing a query. Opening a chip leaves your SQL and Result alone; Enter or Space opens and closes it from the keyboard.

The columns and types describe the table on the active floor, including tables you create. When you replace a table, an open chip refreshes its column view. After switching floors, open the new floor’s chip to inspect that floor’s columns and types.

Use the table chip’s columns and types to choose names for SELECT, WHERE and joins. The column view reads the table quietly: it adds no query to your history or the tutor’s recent queries and never replaces unfinished SQL.

Choose Preview beside any table chip under Tables to see its first 10 rows in a separate panel beside the console, or below it on a narrow screen. Start with trips to see what a row holds. Preview leaves Scratch, Result and query records alone; Close preview takes you back to the chip.

Preview shows up to 10 rows from the table on this floor, including your own outputs. An empty table still shows its column names. Preview refreshes after a replacement and closes when you drop its table or change floors. The panel scrolls sideways for wide rows on a phone.

Preview is a quiet SELECT * with LIMIT 10, without a guaranteed sort order. It does not add a run to either query record. When a transaction is open, Preview explains that you must COMMIT or ROLLBACK before reading rows; it shows columns without running row expressions or changing your transaction.

Use Scratch to explore the given tables or make your own tables. Put one SELECT or WITH query in Answer. Run answer shows its rows in Result; Check floor grades only that query against the original given tables. You do not need to save a table.

Answer uses only this floor’s original given tables, even if you change or drop a table in Scratch. Check floor leaves both boxes, Scratch and Result alone. The task checklist says Answer: not run yet, then shows the row count from your last Run answer; it does not say the answer is correct.

Run answer and Check floor accept the same single SELECT or WITH query. Use Scratch for other statements. Answer text is saved separately for each floor and survives reload, floor switches and Restart floor. Run answer adds an answer entry to both query records; Check floor adds no run.

After Check floor, each failed rule has its own hint ladder: first what is wrong, then an idea and a SQL refresher link, then an inspection query outline with blanks. Further failures stay on rung 3. Hints work with the tutor closed. Passing a rule resets its ladder; passing the floor or Restart floor resets that floor’s ladders.

Check floor advances only the rules that fail: rung 1 explains the problem, rung 2 links an idea to the SQL refresher, and rung 3 gives an inspection query outline with blanks. Complete it in Scratch to investigate; it is not a finished answer. Ladders survive reload and floor switches. A pass or Restart floor resets the relevant ladders, even with the tutor closed.

Each rule has a separate Check floor counter in this browser, capped at rung 3: problem, idea with refresher link, then an inspection outline with blanks. A parser error or refused answer does not advance it. Passing a rule resets that counter; a full pass or Restart floor resets this floor. Other floors keep their counters. The tutor does not control these hints.
